red_full_bodied.recommended_glass: Bordeaux glass with a tall bowl to aerate robust tannins
red_full_bodied.decanting_rationale: Softens youthful astringent tannins and allows concentrated fruit and cedar notes to open

red_light_medium.recommended_glass: Burgundy balloon glass with a wide bowl to collect delicate floral and red fruit aromas
red_light_medium.decanting_rationale: Gentle aeration helps dissipate bottle reduction without losing delicate top aromas

white_crisp.recommended_glass: Narrow U-shaped white wine glass to preserve chilled temperature and concentrate citrus zest
white_crisp.decanting_rationale: Chilling highlights vibrant crisp acidity; decanting is unnecessary and warms the wine prematurely

white_oaked_full.recommended_glass: Wide-mouthed Chardonnay glass allowing creamy mouthfeel and buttery aromas to emerge
white_oaked_full.decanting_rationale: Serving slightly cellar-cool rather than ice-cold reveals secondary oak and toast complexity

rose_dry.recommended_glass: Medium white wine glass with slight taper
rose_dry.decanting_rationale: Best enjoyed fresh and chilled to emphasize lively red fruit and refreshing acidity

sparkling_traditional.recommended_glass: Tulip-shaped glass or white wine glass (preferable over flat coupe) to preserve effervescence and bouquet
sparkling_traditional.decanting_rationale: Decanting releases carbonation too quickly; serve straight from a chilled bottle
